{"body":"**Extension:** Claude Code Extension for Visual Studio 249.0 (VS 2022)

**Environment:** Windows 10 VM (KVM on Fedora host), clipboard shared via Looking Glass, screenshots taken with Flameshot on the host.

**Issue:** Pasting a screenshot into the extension produces a blank (white) image in `ClaudeCodeVS_Session\...\image_N.png`. Pasting the same clipboard in VS Code or other apps works.

**Root cause:** The clipboard contains only opaque 24bpp formats (PNG 24bpp RGB, CF_DIB 24bpp BI_RGB, CF_DIBV5 24bpp with alpha mask 0). WPF `System.Windows.Clipboard.GetImage()` returns a `Bgra32` BitmapSource with **alpha = 0 on every pixel** (555165/555165), so the saved PNG is fully transparent while the RGB data is intact (forcing alpha to 255 restores the image).

**Suggested fix:** prefer the `PNG` clipboard format when present, and/or if the decoded image's alpha channel is entirely 0, force alpha to 255 (or convert to `Bgr32`/24bpp) before saving.

**Workaround:** a clipboard listener that rewrites the image as a 24bpp opaque bitmap + PNG.

content.text: Issue #260 is about clipboard images whose source only offers opaque 24bpp formats. To point you at a useful source, I'll check whether a generated 24bpp clipboard image actually reproduces the bad alpha.

input.content:
Add-Type -AssemblyName System.Drawing
Add-Type -AssemblyName System.Windows.Forms
Add-Type -AssemblyName PresentationCore
Add-Type -AssemblyName WindowsBase

$out = Split-Path -Parent $MyInvocationName
$pngPath = Join-Path $out 'test-24bpp.png'

# Opaque 24bpp bitmap (no alpha channel), similar to what Flameshot/Looking Glass put on the clipboard
$bmp = New-Object System.Drawing.Bitmap 400, 300, ([System.Drawing.Imaging.PixelFormat]::Format24bppRgb)
$g = [System.Drawing.Graphics]::FromImage($bmp)
$g.Clear([System.Drawing.Color]::White)
$g.FillRectangle([System.Drawing.Brushes]::Red, 20, 20, 160, 100)
$g.FillEllipse([System.Drawing.Brushes]::Blue, 200, 120, 160, 140)
$g.Dispose()
$bmp.Save($pngPath, [System.Drawing.Imaging.ImageFormat]::Png)
"Saved 24bpp PNG: $pngPath"

[System.Windows.Forms.Clipboard]::SetImage($bmp)
"Clipboard formats: " + (([System.Windows.Forms.Clipboard]::GetDataObject().GetFormats()) -join ', ')

# Read back the way the extension does (WPF Clipboard.GetImage) and count non-zero alpha pixels
$img = [System.Windows.Clipboard]::GetImage()
if ($null -eq $img) { "WPF GetImage returned null"; return }
"WPF image format: $($img.Format), size: $($img.PixelWidth)x$($img.PixelHeight)"
$bgra = New-Object System.Windows.Media.Imaging.FormatConvertedBitmap $img, ([System.Windows.Media.PixelFormats]::Bgra32), $null, 0
$stride = $bgra.PixelWidth * 4
$buf = New-Object byte[] ($stride * $bgra.PixelHeight)
$bgra.CopyPixels($buf, $stride, 0)
$nonZero = 0
for ($i = 3; $i -lt $buf.Length; $i += 4) { if ($buf[$i] -ne 0) { $nonZero++ } }
"Pixels with alpha != 0: $nonZero of $($bgra.PixelWidth * $bgra.PixelHeight)"

content.text: The save failed because `$MyInvocationName` is empty under `-File`, and the clipboard test used WinForms' bitmap path, which came back fully opaque. That doesn't reproduce the bug. I'll build a raw 24bpp CF_DIB, which matches the issue's clipboard contents, and retry.

input.content:
Add-Type -AssemblyName System.Drawing
Add-Type -AssemblyName System.Windows.Forms
Add-Type -AssemblyName PresentationCore
Add-Type -AssemblyName WindowsBase

$out = $PSScriptRoot
$pngPath = Join-Path $out 'test-24bpp.png'
$w = 400
$h = 300

# Raw 24bpp BI_RGB DIB: top half red, bottom half blue (DIB rows are bottom-up, BGR order, rows padded to 4 bytes)
$rowBytes = [int](([int]$w * 3 + 3) / 4) * 4
$pixels = New-Object byte[] ($rowBytes * $h)
for ($y = 0; $y -lt $h; $y++) {
    for ($x = 0; $x -lt $w; $x++) {
        $o = ($h - 1 - $y) * $rowBytes + $x * 3
        if ($y -lt $h / 2) { $pixels[$o] = 0; $pixels[$o + 1] = 0; $pixels[$o + 2] = 255 }   # red
        else { $pixels[$o] = 255; $pixels[$o + 1] = 0; $pixels[$o + 2] = 0 }                 # blue
    }
}
$header = New-Object byte[] 40
[BitConverter]::GetBytes([int]40).CopyTo($header, 0)
[BitConverter]::GetBytes([int]$w).CopyTo($header, 4)
[BitConverter]::GetBytes([int]$h).CopyTo($header, 8)
[BitConverter]::GetBytes([int16]1).CopyTo($header, 12)
[BitConverter]::GetBytes([int16]24).CopyTo($header, 14)
[BitConverter]::GetBytes([int]($rowBytes * $h)).CopyTo($header, 20)
$dib = New-Object byte[] ($header.Length + $pixels.Length)
$header.CopyTo($dib, 0)
$pixels.CopyTo($dib, $header.Length)

# Same pixels as an opaque 24bpp PNG file (mirrors the issue's "PNG 24bpp RGB" clipboard entry)
$bmp = New-Object System.Drawing.Bitmap $w, $h, ([System.Drawing.Imaging.PixelFormat]::Format24bppRgb)
$rect = New-Object System.Drawing.Rectangle 0, 0, $w, $h
$data = $bmp.LockBits($rect, [System.Drawing.Imaging.ImageLockMode]::WriteOnly, $bmp.PixelFormat)
for ($y = 0; $y -lt $h; $y++) {
    [System.Runtime.InteropServices.Marshal]::Copy($pixels, ($h - 1 - $y) * $rowBytes, [IntPtr]($data.Scan0.ToInt64() + $y * $data.Stride), $w * 3)
}
$bmp.UnlockBits($data)
$bmp.Save($pngPath, [System.Drawing.Imaging.ImageFormat]::Png)
"Saved 24bpp PNG: $pngPath"

# Put only the opaque 24bpp DIB on the clipboard
$ms = New-Object System.IO.MemoryStream (, $dib)
$obj = New-Object System.Windows.Forms.DataObject
$obj.SetData('DeviceIndependentBitmap', $ms)
[System.Windows.Forms.Clipboard]::SetDataObject($obj, $true)
"Clipboard formats: " + (([System.Windows.Forms.Clipboard]::GetDataObject().GetFormats()) -join ', ')

# Read back the way the extension does (WPF Clipboard.GetImage) and count non-zero alpha pixels
$img = [System.Windows.Clipboard]::GetImage()
if ($null -eq $img) { "WPF GetImage returned null"; return }
"WPF image format: $($img.Format), size: $($img.PixelWidth)x$($img.PixelHeight)"
$bgra = New-Object System.Windows.Media.Imaging.FormatConvertedBitmap $img, ([System.Windows.Media.PixelFormats]::Bgra32), $null, 0
$stride = $bgra.PixelWidth * 4
$buf = New-Object byte[] ($stride * $bgra.PixelHeight)
$bgra.CopyPixels($buf, $stride, 0)
$nonZero = 0
for ($i = 3; $i -lt $buf.Length; $i += 4) { if ($buf[$i] -ne 0) { $nonZero++ } }
"Pixels with alpha != 0: $nonZero of $($bgra.PixelWidth * $bgra.PixelHeight)"

content.text:
You don't need a special screenshot. Issue #260 needs a clipboard that holds only an opaque 24bpp image, and I generated one that reproduces the bug.

Run this script:

`C:\Temp\Windows\claude\C--GitLab-ClaudeCodeExtension\42c988a8-9ab0-4a24-98ef-43824fa1a3d1\scratchpad\make-24bpp-clipboard.ps1`

It puts a raw 24bpp DIB on the clipboard (red top half, blue bottom half) and reads it back the way the extension does with WPF `Clipboard.GetImage()`. The result was:

```
Clipboard formats: DeviceIndependentBitmap
WPF image format: Bgra32, size: 400x300
Pixels with alpha != 0: 0 of 120000
```

Every pixel has alpha 0, so the bug reproduces. The image should still be on your clipboard now. Paste it into the extension's prompt to test. Before a fix, the saved PNG is fully transparent. After a fix, it should show red over blue. If you copy something else first, rerun the script.

Two things to know:
- A bitmap set through the normal .NET `Clipboard.SetImage` path did not reproduce; the raw DIB is what matters.
- The script covers only the DIB-only case. The issue also mentions a PNG 24bpp clipboard entry, and the suggested fix prefers that format. I can add a PNG entry to the script if you want to test that path too.

The reporter got their image from a Flameshot screenshot shared into a Windows VM through Looking Glass. The script stands in for that setup.

Also, issue #260 has a repo-watcher claim comment from today (10:20 UTC), so someone may already be working on a fix.
